quotes.text: In the meeting just concluded, the FOMC decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point to 3¾ to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve’s dual mandate.
The plain fact is that inflation is too high and has been for too long.
The committee’s unanimous vote shows our resolve to achieve price stability on a timelier basis.
I'm not going to pre-judge any future decisions we make.
I care so much, I think it's so important, that we established a task force that should report by the end of the year to help us think about the implications for our future policy conjuncture.

evidence.fragment: decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point to 3¾ to 4 percent

summary.text: Chairman Warsh said the FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point to 3¾ to 4 percent and is maintaining ample reserves.

evidence.fragment: economic activity is expanding at a solid pace. While uncertainty remains elevated

summary.text: Warsh said economic activity is expanding at a solid pace, but inflation remains elevated, and said the action would support a timelier return to the Committee’s 2 percent goal.

evidence.fragment: real GDP rises at 2.3 percent this year and 2.4 percent next year

summary.text: Warsh said the Committee’s median projections show real GDP rising at 2.3 percent this year and 2.4 percent next year, while total PCE inflation falls from 3.7 percent to 2.3 percent.

evidence.fragment: I'm not in the forward guidance business.

summary.text: Warsh said he was not in the forward guidance business and would not pre-judge any future decisions.

evidence.fragment: the economy has strengthened. You might have heard me say that in Jackson Hole

summary.text: Warsh said the Committee’s judgment had changed since July because the economy had strengthened, inflation information had not changed his view, and geopolitics had changed.

evidence.fragment: we established a task force that should report by the end of the year

summary.text: Warsh said the Federal Reserve established a task force to report by the end of the year to help it think about implications for its future policy conjuncture.

summaries.title: Federal Reserve press conference transcript, 16 September 2026

quotes.text: Three-month inflation has fallen steadily from 4.76 percent in February. That is a considerable improvement, and the speed of this downward trajectory is encouraging.
If there is continued progress toward our 2 percent goal, then I am willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level.
But if inflation comes in hot, I would consider a rate hike.
The key point here is that this it is not a commitment to a policy action—it is a conditional policy statement.

evidence.fragment: I expect real GDP to grow a bit more than 2 percent this year

summary.text: Governor Waller says real GDP grew at a 1.8 percent annual rate in the first half of this year, and Governor Waller expects real GDP to grow a bit more than 2 percent this year.

evidence.fragment: Job creation, though a bit volatile, has increased this year by an average of 60,000 a month through July.

summary.text: Governor Waller says job creation has increased this year by an average of 60,000 a month through July, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent in July.

evidence.fragment: Three-month inflation has fallen steadily from 4.76 percent in February.

summary.text: Governor Waller says PCE prices are up 3.7 percent in the past 12 months and core PCE inflation is 3.3 percent, while three-month core inflation fell from 4.76 percent in February to 3.05 percent through July.

evidence.fragment: If there is continued progress toward our 2 percent goal, then I am willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level.

summary.text: Governor Waller says that, if August data show continued progress toward the 2 percent goal, he is willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level; if inflation comes in hot, he would consider a rate hike.

evidence.fragment: The third and final type of communication is forward guidance, which specifies a path for the policy rate that is essentially independent of incoming data.

summary.text: Governor Waller says he communicates his current policy position, his reaction function for how future data would shape decisions, and forward guidance when it is truly needed.

summaries.title: Waller, The Economic Outlook and Some Comments on My Policy Communication
